full_judgment:
Md Delwar Hossain J: This Rule was issued on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceeding of Special Tribunal Case No. 96 of 2003 corresponding to GR No. 12 of 2003 arising out of Joydebpur Police Station Case No. 10 dated 8-1-2003 under section 25C(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 pending in the Senior Special Tribunal No. 4, Gazipur should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. On the basis of the first information report Joydebpur Police Station Case No. 10 dated 8-1-2003 was recorded under section 25C (b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 against all the accuseds including the accused petitioners. Police concluding the investigation submitted charge sheet on 30-5-2003 against all the accuseds including the accused petitioners under section 25C(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. Thereafter the case record was transmit-ted to the Special Tribunal, Gazipur and registered as Special Tribunal Case No. 96 of 2003. The learned Judge of the Tribunal taking cognizance against all the accuseds transferred the case record to the Special Tribunal No. 3, Gazipur for trial and disposal. In the meantime the accused petitioners were enlarged on bail on 5-4-2003 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4542 of 2003 and on 27-8-2003 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 11172 of 2003 respectively by the High Court Division. 

 5. The accused petitioners being aggrieved with the continuation of the proceeding of the case moved this Court with this application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the proceeding and obtained this Rule on 5-7-2004. At the time of issuance of the Rule the entire proceedings of the case was stayed. 

 9. Before entering into merit of the case it would be proper to quote here section 25C(1) (b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 for better understanding which reads as under : 

 10. Reading the provisions of law as provided in section 25C(1)(b) quoted above, it appears that an accused may be punished if he is found guilty for the offence of adulteration of or sale of adulterated food, drink, drugs or cosmetics only. In the instant proceeding the allegation against the accused petitioners is that they adulterated fertiliser for sale which definitely does not come within the mischief of section 25C(1)(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. 

 11. The allegations brought against the accused petitioners for adulteration of and/or sale of adulterated fertiliser do not constitute any criminal offence within the purview of section 25C(1)(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. Since no prima facie case has been made out against the accused petitioners it will be a sheer harassment to them to face a baseless criminal proceeding. 

 12. The cardinal principles of criminal jurisprudence is that no one should be harassed in a criminal proceeding when the allegations made out do not constitute any criminal offence. The allegations made in the first information report and the charge sheet against the accused petitioners do not prima facie constitute any criminal offence as provided in section 25C (1)(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. The learned Judge of the Tribunal misconstruing and misreading the provisions of section 25C (1)(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 framed charge thereunder against the accused petitioners. 

 13. Since the allegations made in the first information report and the charge sheet do not constitute any criminal offence against these accused petitioners within the mischief of section 25C(1)(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 the proceeding of the said case will be an abuse of process of the court and the same cannot be allowed to continue against them. 

 15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The proceeding of Special Tribunal Case No.96 of 2003 pending before the Special Tribunal No.4, Gazipur under section 25C(1)(b) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 is quashed so far as it relates to the accused petitioners.
